engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Thinking Process
chess.body: Every move: 1. What did my opponent just do? (threats?) 2. What are my candidate moves? (at least 2-3) 3. Calculate each candidate 2-3 moves deep. 4. Use LPDO check. 5. Make the move. Don't play on impulse. Even 30 seconds of structured thinking eliminates 80% of blunders. This process is the difference between 800 and 1200 Elo.

wisdom.title: On Anger
wisdom.body: Anger is information, not instruction. It tells you a boundary was crossed or a value was violated. But acting on anger rarely solves the problem. Practice: when you feel it rising, say 'I need 5 minutes' and leave the room. Return calm. Then address the issue. You can be firm without being explosive.

book.author: Charlie Munger
book.chapter: Mental Models: Think in Multiple Frameworks
book.lesson: Charlie Munger's approach to decision-making: build a 'latticework of mental models' from multiple disciplines. The person who only knows accounting sees every problem through accounting. The person who knows psychology, economics, biology, physics, and history sees the problem in full. Munger's rule: you need 80-90 mental models to think well. The key ones: compound interest (mathematics), evolution (biology), supply and demand (economics), confirmation bias (psychology), systems thinking (engineering). His most important: 'I never allow myself to have an opinion I can't defend with the strongest arguments on the other side.'
book.key_quote: The person with one framework is fragile. The person with many frameworks is antifragile — they see what others miss.
book.action: Pick one field outside finance to study this month: psychology, history, or biology. Look for one principle that applies directly to your FP&A work.
crux: Build a latticework of mental models from many disciplines. One-model thinking distorts every problem.
To the man with a hammer, every problem looks like a nail. Most professionals are that man.
Invert, always invert. Ask how to fail, then avoid that.
Know your circle of competence and stay inside it. The edge is knowing where the edge ends.
Incentives explain most behaviour. Look at the incentive before assuming intent.
The psychology of misjudgement runs about 25 standard biases. Learn them as a checklist.
Opportunity cost is the correct filter for every decision.
Sit on your hands. Great opportunities are rare; act rarely and heavily.
Avoid the three big destroyers: alcohol, leverage, and envy. Envy is the stupidest.
Multiply models: compound interest, scale, backup systems, breakpoints, critical mass.
A great business at a fair price beats a fair business at a great price.
Read constantly. Neither Munger nor Buffett knows a wise person who doesn't read all the time.
Be reliable. Unreliability cancels every virtue you have.
Take a simple idea and take it seriously. That is the whole method.
learnings: Avoiding stupidity beats seeking brilliance, and it is far more achievable.
Inversion surfaces risks that forward thinking never reaches.
Most bad decisions come from one model applied where it doesn't fit.
Patience is a strategy, not a personality trait.
examples: Munger's Costco analysis combines scale economics, incentive design, and psychology at once — no single-discipline read explains it.
See's Candies: Berkshire paid up for brand pricing power in 1972 and it returned over $2bn on a $25m outlay.
Munger rebuilt from a divorce, no money, and the death of his 9-year-old son to become a billionaire. Reliability compounded.
adapt: Invert the Dubai plan: what guarantees no offer by mid-2026? Then remove those causes.
Circle of competence: Indian equities and FP&A. Polymarket stays paper-only until 200 trades say otherwise.
Check incentives before trusting any financial content, including your own.
Sit on your hands when the regime filter says no. Not trading is a position.

minimalism.title: The Someday Pile
minimalism.body: 'I'll fix it someday.' 'I'll read it someday.' Someday is not a date. The pile is not a to-do list, it is a monument to intentions you have already declined.
minimalism.action: Give every someday item a date this month, or let it go today.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Ramadan Awareness
etiquette.body: Do not eat, drink, or smoke in public during fasting hours. Schedule meetings earlier. Expect shortened hours. Wishing colleagues Ramadan Kareem costs nothing and is noticed.
etiquette.action: Check the Islamic calendar. Know what month it is.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Attention Is The Life
stillness.body: What you pay attention to is, quite literally, your experience of being alive. Spend it on what you would choose to have lived through.
stillness.action: Audit yesterday's screen time. That number is a portion of your life.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Margin Of Safety
model.body: Build the bridge for 30 tonnes and drive 10 across it. Applies to leverage, deadlines, cash buffers, and assumptions in a model. The error is always in the direction you did not plan for.
model.action: Add 50% buffer to your next estimate. Do not tell yourself it is padding.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.use: Disarming and appreciated. The effort matters far more than the fluency.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Write The Email In Three Lines
drill.body: Context, ask, deadline. Long emails do not get read, they get postponed. Brevity is a service to the reader and it gets you answers faster.
drill.action: Rewrite your longest pending email in three lines.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Sitting Is Not The New Smoking, But
health.body: Prolonged uninterrupted sitting impairs glucose handling regardless of whether you exercised that day. The fix is frequency of interruption, not total exercise volume.
health.action: Stand or walk 2 minutes every 30. Set a timer for one work block.
health.label: Health

case.title: Berkshire Hathaway: Float as a Business Model
case.story: Buffett uses insurance float — money collected in premiums before claims — as free capital to invest. $160B float generates investment returns at zero cost.
case.lesson: The best business models create free capital. Study how your industry's best companies actually make money — it's rarely where you think.

fpna.title: Working Capital
fpna.body: DSO + DIO – DPO = Cash Conversion Cycle. Cutting CCC by 5 days can free millions.

cfo.title: Dubai FC Reality
cfo.body: AED 30K+ FC roles at ADNOC, Emirates, MAF, DP World: they want Big 4 background OR 8+ years in a listed company + CA/ACCA + ERP experience. Your edge: FP&A depth + IFRS knowledge + Power BI automation. Highlight cost savings you drove.

money_hack.title: Direct Funds Only
money_hack.body: Regular mutual funds cost 1–1.5% more per year. Over 20 years = 30% of corpus gone.

dubai.title: Six weeks, not six months
dubai.body: Government-linked groups take three to six months from application to offer. Private groups take four to eight weeks. Applying only to the first kind and then reading the silence as rejection is the most common way this search dies.
dubai.targets: Run both pipelines at once. The fast one funds the patience for the slow one.
dubai.action: One sheet: company, date applied, stage, next action, date of next action.

desk.productivity: Respond to messages at set times. Real-time response is a myth.

father.title: Introduce one new texture
father.do: Let her touch something unfamiliar and safe — a cold spoon, a rough towel, wet cloth.
father.why: Sensory variety builds neural discrimination. At this age the mouth is a primary sense organ, so expect it to be tasted; choose accordingly.

father.title: Sing badly and often
father.do: One song, daily, the same one. Tune is irrelevant.
father.why: Melody carries language patterns — rhythm, stress, phrase boundaries — more clearly than speech. She is not judging the singing.

life_wisdom.teaching: Once a year, at Michchhami Dukkadam, Jains ask forgiveness of everyone they may have harmed — regardless of whether they feel at fault.
life_wisdom.apply: The ritual removes the negotiation over who was more wrong. Do not wait for the annual version: close a grudge this week without settling the scoreboard first.

life_wisdom.teaching: 'In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities; in the expert's there are few.' Expertise narrows the field of what you consider.
life_wisdom.apply: In your area of deepest expertise, ask the question you would find embarrassing to ask. Ten years in one industry is where assumptions calcify.

speaking.title: Record and listen back
speaking.drill: Record 60 seconds answering 'why do you want to be a CFO?'. Listen once for content, once for delivery only.
speaking.why: Almost nobody does this, and it is the single fastest improvement available. You will hear things no one will tell you.

interview_tech.q: How do you evaluate a capex request for store refurbishment versus a new store?
interview_tech.a: Both need incremental cash flow, but the counterfactual differs. For a new store, the baseline is zero. For a refurbishment, the baseline is the store's declining trajectory without investment — so the benefit is the uplift over that decline, not over today. People systematically overstate refurbishment returns by comparing post-refit sales to pre-refit sales, which double-counts the natural trend and any category resets. Ask for the do-nothing case in writing.

interview_tech.q: What is the one number you would put on a retail CEO's daily dashboard?
interview_tech.a: Like-for-like sales versus plan, with gross margin rate alongside it. One without the other is dangerous — sales up on margin collapse is a discount habit forming, and margin up on sales collapse is a range problem. If forced to a single figure, gross profit versus plan, because it moves only when something real happens. Everything else — footfall, conversion, basket, density — is diagnostic detail you reach for once that number moves.

interview_soft.q: Describe a time you had to deliver bad news to senior stakeholders.
interview_soft.a: Lead with the structure you used, because that is the skill. Bad news goes: the number, the cause, the impact, the plan, the ask. No preamble. Deliver it early even when incomplete — 'here is what I know now and what I will know Friday' beats a complete answer a week late. Give a specific example with the actual figure and what you did next. The tell they look for: did you surface it or did someone else find it.

interview_soft.q: Why should we hire you over a candidate with Big Four and listed-company experience?
interview_soft.a: Do not disparage the alternative. Frame the trade: audit teaches you to verify what happened; operating finance teaches you to change what happens next. Then be specific about what you own that they do not — a live multi-country P&L, an ERP implementation you led rather than advised on, and store-level decisions you made and were held to. End with the honest gap and how you would close it. Confidence with a named weakness beats confidence alone.
